newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cantor Fitzgerald expands in Frankfurt for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Cantor Fitzgerald expands in Frankfurt for EMU.

text.p: U.S. brokerage Cantor Fitzgerald International said late on Wednesday it would expand its operations in Frankfurt in preparation for the planned launch of Europe's single currency in January 1999.

The brokerage, which opened a branch in the German financial capital at the end of 1996, plans to move its Bund trading team to Frankfurt from London and also focus on global sales of Pfandbriefe, which are mortgage-backed and local government bonds peculiar to the German market.
Cantor Fitzgerald President, Howard Lutnick, told a press briefing the company would invest around $10 million a year for the next three years in the Frankfurt branch.
Plans were in place for 80 jobs in the city within two years, Lutnick said.
"In three or four years that could be 150," he said.
In the longer term, Cantor Fitzgerald aimed to generate half its global business in Europe. The region currently accounts for about a third of the broker's business.
